A.explanation: Y cannot be speed because speed starts at $0$, while Y starts at a maximum value.

B.explanation: X cannot be height because X falls to zero with zero gradient, which would mean landing with zero speed.

C.explanation: Y is height, Z is speed rising to terminal velocity, and X is resultant force falling from $mg$ to zero.

D.explanation: Z cannot be height because height starts at the building height, while Z starts at $0$.

hints: Notice the starting values at $t = 0$: the dropped object has zero speed but maximum height and maximum resultant force $mg$.
Recall that with significant air resistance speed rises from $0$ with decreasing gradient toward terminal velocity as drag grows.
Connect resultant force $mg - \text{drag}$ to speed: it is largest at $t = 0$ and tends to zero, while height falls with an increasingly steep negative gradient.
walkthrough: At $t = 0$ the object is dropped from rest, so speed $= 0$, height $=$ building height, and drag $= 0$ so resultant force $= mg$ is maximum.
Graph Z starts at $0$ and rises with decreasing gradient to a constant value. This matches speed increasing with decreasing acceleration toward terminal velocity.
Graph Y starts at a maximum and falls with an increasingly negative gradient. This matches height above the ground, since the downward speed is increasing so height is lost faster.
Graph X starts at a maximum and falls to zero. This matches magnitude of resultant force $mg - \text{drag}$, which is $mg$ at $t = 0$ and decreases to near zero as drag approaches weight.
Therefore Y is height, Z is speed, and X is resultant force. This is option C.
